title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: TiDEomics R package designed streamline analysis time-course omics data (e.g. proteomics, transcriptomics), compatible single group analysis multiple group comparison, accommodating data missing values. tutorial demonstrates basic workflow, explains key parameters, gives practical tips. Key features covered: Preparing input - Create SummarizedExperiment object data matrix sample annotation, checks correct formatting. Quality control - Check value distributions missingness patterns. Normalisation, grouping merging replicates - Normalise feature starting time point focused changes baseline. Transform data analyses require single groups single time series. Sample relationships visualisation (correlation matrix, PCA, UMAP) - Explore global structure major sources variance, check batch effects, identify features driving PCs. Pairwise differential expression (time group) - Identify DE features pairs time points within group, pairs groups time point. Classification feature property (randomness overall fold change) - Classify features different categories (e.g., non-random vs. random, differentially expressed vs. stable) based properties including trend significance maximum fold change. Segmented regression Trendy - Estimate breakpoints feature group summarise dynamic patterns. Variance decomposition modified PALMO - Quantify relative contributions Time, Group, Residual, distinguish time group-dependent DE features “noisy” features. Module identification WGCNA - Identify co-expression modules different temporal group-specific patterns. Functional enrichment (gene ontology, drugs) - Interpret biological meaning identified DE features modules.

Sample: matches column names data Group: experimental group Time: numeric time point Replicate: replicate id (optional) Batch: batch id (optional) Example: subset GSE263759 data set published Traxler et al. (2025). Ensembl IDs mapped symbols, genes zero counts excluded. Use time 0 untreated samples groups’ time 0. Sample 500 random genes. title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: two DE functions pairwise comparison time points groups based limma package (Ritchie et al. 2015). DE_between_time(): Compares pairs time points within group. Output: list features, list significant features. Separate plotting function: plot_DE_between_time() summarise number DE features per time point per group. DE_between_group(): Compares pairs groups time point. Output: list features, list significant features, line plots summarising number DE features (can removed setting plot = FALSE). Common parameters functions: assay: index assay use (1 = original, 2 = time0-normalised available) filter: minimal number non-NA observations/replicates per feature included DE testing (e.g., filter = 1 means requiring features least 1 non-NA value time points group). Default thresholds DE p.adj < 0.05 |log2FC| > 1. Please note example data two replicates per time point. replicates recommended robust pairwise DE analysis. text: calc_feature_property() computes per-feature properties: P_trend calculated randtests::bartels.rank.test() test non-randomness time profile (.e., whether feature shows significant overall trend across time points). Max_FC: maximum fold change across time points, calculated difference maximum minimum mean abundance across time points. captures overall magnitude change across time course, regardless specific time points changes occur. Max_FC_time: difference time points maximum minimum mean abundance, providing information direction () duration changing. Exp_threshold: user-set value threshold feature considered expressed sample. can used filter features based expression level, e.g. setting threshold = 0 means values > 0 (log2(raw count + 1) > 0, .e. raw count > 0) considered expressed. default NULL, means non-NA values considered expressed, e.g. proteomics data. T_total, T_exp Exp_ratio: number total time points, number expressed time points values > Exp_threshold (non-NA values threshold = NULL), proportion expressed time points, respectively, can used filter features based completeness expression level. property values can used classify features different categories (e.g., non-random vs. random, differentially expressed vs. stable) downstream analysis interpretation. example, features P_trend < 0.05 Max_FC >= 1 can candidates non-randomly overall-changing DE features.
